findings.title: A cancelled native read cannot leave publication-monitor acquisition
findings.reasoning: Every ordinary query on a text-backed dataset enters SearchDeltaJournal.captureRead before creating its QueryExec. ReadCapture acquires the shared qualified monitor with Java synchronized. ReadBoundary.cancel only interrupts the worker and aborts a registered execution; there is no execution yet while this monitor is being acquired. Intrinsic monitor acquisition does not respond to interruption. A writer holding publicationMonitor through commit/qualification can therefore retain an expired or disconnected servlet worker beyond the required 300 ms native release grace. The check inside the begin callback runs only after the monitor becomes available. Main/proxy transport release cannot free this native waiter.

relatedLocations.reason: Cancellation interrupts the worker and invokes only an already registered engine abort.
Cancellation check runs after acquiring the capture monitor.
publicationMonitor is the same qualified monitor used by capture.
Intrinsic monitor acquisition has no deadline/cancellation-aware wait.
Writer retains this monitor across commit, dataset end and bounded qualification.
Readiness/delta proof uses the same capture path; its default begin callback has no ReadBoundary check.
Default capture starts its READ transaction after monitor acquisition.
SlowData is a transaction-memory fixture; engine work blocks using interruptible sleep, without a contended text publication monitor.

findings.classReach: Ordinary SPARQL reads on the text-backed dataset and native command capture consumers, including delta-readiness and exact-unit probes. The separate template engine watch does not repair capture-lock waiting.
findings.outcomeImpact: Departed readers can continue occupying native servlet capacity until publication finishes. A readiness capture may also begin its transaction after cancellation once the monitor becomes free. No unauthorized disclosure or executed regression is claimed.
findings.whyExistingAssertionsDoNotDisprove: RequestReadBoundaryTest exercises a SlowData engine fixture after query entry; it does not hold the real publication monitor or prove cleanup while a writer remains inside it. The composition case observes upstream proxy transports only.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Make publication/capture acquisition deadline- and cancellation-aware while preserving the atomic RDF/Lucene cut. Refuse the wait without starting a transaction or engine after expiry. Do not bypass or split the existing publication fence.
findings.proposedFalsification: Add a focused native case that holds the publication monitor longer than the grace, starts a real text-backed ordinary query or readiness capture, then expires or cancels it. Assert native request work exits within 300 ms while the holder is still held, no transaction/engine starts after departure, and an independent fresh read succeeds after release. This is a proposed follow-up, not an executed failure or a replacement for the manager prove selection.
